newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU adds 35 million Ecus to "mad cow" research funds.
newsitem.headline: EU adds 35 million Ecus to "mad cow" research funds.

text.p: The Research Council agreed on Thursday to add 35 million Ecus to the funds available for research into fatal brain-wasting diseases such as mad cow disease and its human equivalent.

The extra funds, still to be cleared by the European Parliament under the co-decision procedure, are part of a package of extra cash worth 100 million European currency units for projects related to multimedia software for education, land mine destruction, water, environment, aerospace and transport.

Research into mad-cow-type diseases became a priority for the EU after British scientists last March raised the possibility that humans could develop the human equivalent of bovine spongiform encephalopahty (BSE) by eating infected beef.
The revelation led to a world-wide ban on beef and derived products from Britain, where 165,000 cattle have developed BSE in the last 10 years.

"I have no doubt that news of new, additional funding for research on this important topic will be welcomed by consumer, agriculture and health interests and will also act to restore consumer confidence," Irish Research Minister Pat Rabbitte told a news conference after the Council.

The decision was delayed several hours by Italy's insistence that there be a reference to funds available for car-related projects within the financial supplement to the fourth framework RTD programme.

In the end, ministers maintained the allocations drawn up ahead of the meeting, allocating 35 million Ecus to transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (TSEs), 20 million for aeronautics research, 12 million for educational multimedia, 12 million for inter-modal transport, 12 million for projects related to water and the environment and nine million for research related to land mines.
Research related to vaccines and viral diseases was bundled with the TSE money, a European Commission official said.

Ministers also agreed their TSE conclusions which included the agreement to transfer a further 9.8 million Ecus of the original budget to the existing 5.9 million Ecus earmarked for such research in the fourth framework programme.

Ministers also adopted conclusions on using research to help the fight against illegal drug use and another set of conclusions encouraging the participation of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in EU research activities.
Ministers also adopted conclusions on the role of the Joint Research Centre and a decision on the science and technology agreement with South Africa, as detailed in proposal COM(96)423.
